short: Fifty years of war with France, plague at home, and the rise of Parliament's purse.
full:
Edward III came to the throne at fourteen after his mother Isabella and Roger Mortimer deposed his father, and seized power for himself in a coup at Nottingham in 1330. From 1337 he pressed a claim to the French crown, beginning the Hundred Years War, and won a run of victories at Sluys in 1340, Crecy in 1346 and Poitiers in 1356, where his son the Black Prince captured King John II.

The Treaty of Bretigny in 1360 gave him Aquitaine in full sovereignty in exchange for dropping the French title, but war resumed in 1369 and most of the gains were lost. The Black Death killed perhaps a third of the population from 1348, and the Statute of Labourers tried and failed to hold wages down. Paying for the war made the king dependent on parliamentary taxation, and the Commons emerged as a distinct body with its own speaker. Edward died at Sheen in 1377 after years of decline.
